title: Controllable Latent Diffusion for Traffic Simulation

control_signal.value: A designer-specified reward/cost on generated trajectories; the paper's rewards are no-collision and no-off-road (reward -1 on violation, else 0), weighted in a cost J.

control_mechanism.value: Denoising is treated as a multi-step MDP; the latent diffusion model is trained with a policy-gradient using importance sampling, with reward computed on decoded trajectories.

base_model.value: LSTM-based VAE with CNN context encoder for latent compression, plus a context-conditioned latent diffusion model trained with the VAE decoder and dynamics function.

datasets.value: nuScenes; closed-loop simulation initialised from ground-truth states, 20 s with 2 Hz re-planning.

metrics.value: Realism: mean Wasserstein distance of longitudinal acceleration, lateral acceleration and jerk distributions. Stability: failure rate (collision or off-road).

controllability_evidence.value: Ablation: with RL guidance failure rates are 0.226 (no collision) and 0.136 (no off-road); without it they rise to 0.483 and 0.450.

stated_limitations.value: Without reward guidance the realism metric is better (0.350 vs 0.655) but failure rates rise, so a realism/controllability trade-off exists. Future work: wider safety-critical scenarios, other agent types.

notes: Only collision and off-road rewards are demonstrated, so 'controllability' is essentially constraint satisfaction. Baseline numbers in Table I are quoted from another paper. Abstract calls 0.226 a collision rate; Results call it a failure rate.
